mechanism: When banks tighten C&I lending standards to small firms, credit-dependent activity slows and recession/earnings risk rises; equity exposure should be reduced when net-tightening is high or rising. SLOOS historically leads the cycle by ~1-4 quarters.
key_finding: Best search-phase rule uses level at L3q with OOS Sharpe 1.51 versus buy-and-hold 0.89.
caveats: Quarterly survey with a small OOS window — winner is search-selected, needs holdout validation.
SLOOS is NSA and revised; the survey is qualitative (net-% of banks), not a hard activity measure.
Credit-tightening episodes are few, so the lead estimate rests on a handful of cycles.
narrative_summary: SLOOS C&I small-firm tightening is tested as a leading credit-stress overlay for SPY — reduce exposure when banks tighten.

known_stress_episodes.label: Dot-Com recession
known_stress_episodes.note: Tightening rose ahead of the downturn.
